title: Persona Generators: Generating Diverse Synthetic Personas at Scale

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary optimization of LLM-based synthetic persona generators for behavioral diversity coverage
mechanism.populationDetail: AlphaEvolve runs ten independent islands seeded round-robin from three initial Persona Generator implementations.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each island tracks separate elite generator code for each of six diversity metrics, up to 60 metric-specific elites overall; these are not descriptor-cell QD elites.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Metric-specific elite generators are retained; approximately every eight hours/100 iterations, poorly performing islands are reset using solutions copied from better-performing islands. The standard within-island AlphaEvolve survivor update is not detailed.
mechanism.generationDetail: AlphaEvolve mutates an existing Persona Generator codebase, potentially changing logic in either internal stage while preserving the two-stage architecture and ordering.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The mutation operator receives a random subset of persona profiles paired with questionnaire-response scores; six population diversity metrics form the fitness vector and per-metric elite criteria.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The paper describes island seeding, per-metric elite tracking, and periodic reset sources, but not the exact parent-selection rule for each mutation. Avoid asserting score-based or top-k sampling as the universal rule.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The optimized candidate is a reusable generator function with an inner two-stage population synthesis architecture: autoregressive population-level diversity positioning followed by parallel persona expansion. This nested generator design is distinct from the outer evolutionary parent-offspring mechanism.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Persona Generators Generating Diverse Synthetic Personas at Scale.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The paper is cited in the application/social-simulation discussion but not yet in mechanism-taxonomy prose. Per-metric elites and scheduled island resets support multi-elite/island labels, but standard within-island AlphaEvolve replacement and parent selection are not specified. Monte Carlo approximation applies specifically to the coverage metric.
